subject: physics
question_text: Which physical quantity remains constant (i) in an elastic collision (ii) in an inelastic collision?

verification.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024), Unit 6 VERY SHORT ANSWER. The 1+1 mark split is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher; no exam appearance years are printed for this question, so appearances[] stays empty. The TSBIE Basic Learning Material has no VSAQ section for this unit, so the Fastrack is the only source for it.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: (i) Elastic
lines: both the total linear momentum AND the
steps.margin_note: Say BOTH. Naming only one is the commonest way to lose this mark.
steps.why: Elastic means nothing is left behind as heat or sound, so the kinetic energy the bodies had is still kinetic energy afterwards.
common_mistakes: Writing only "kinetic energy" and forgetting momentum.

recall.must_convey: That in an elastic collision both momentum and kinetic energy stay constant.

steps.memory_tip: Elastic keeps BOTH: momentum and kinetic energy.

steps.label: (ii) Inelastic

lines.text: only the total momentum is constant.

lines: Some kinetic energy becomes heat, sound
or deformation, so KE is not conserved.
steps.margin_note: Say where the kinetic energy went. "Not conserved" alone reads like a guess.
steps.why: Momentum survives every collision because the forces are internal. Kinetic energy does not, because it can be converted into other forms.
common_mistakes: Saying momentum is lost too. Momentum is conserved in EVERY collision.

recall.must_convey: That in an inelastic collision only momentum stays constant, kinetic energy does not.

steps.memory_tip: Inelastic keeps momentum only — some kinetic energy leaves as heat, sound and deformation.

insider_note: Part (i) is one mark for TWO quantities, momentum and kinetic energy. Naming only one loses the whole mark, not half of it.
